name: Statement of Facts
title: Statement of Facts

legal_basis.note: The cause of action must be substantially indicated

An admission is a statement suggesting an inference as to a fact in issue, and is evidence against the party who makes it. This restates the principle formerly in S.17 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872; the corresponding section of the Adhiniyam must be confirmed against the bare Act.

source: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023; Civil Procedure Code, 1908
statutory_reference: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 - section to be confirmed; Civil Procedure Code, 1908 - S.80(3)
authoring_note: The facts in a notice are pleaded facts in all but name. They will be put to the sender in cross-examination and a departure from them at trial is damaging, so the notice should state only what the client can prove and should not overstate. Dates, amounts and document references belong here; characterisation and adjectives do not.
statute_currency: CITATION OUT OF DATE. The Indian Evidence Act, 1872 was repealed with effect from 1 July 2024 by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. The principle relied on here survives the repeal, but the SECTION NUMBER does not carry across - the Adhiniyam renumbered throughout. Published correspondence tables circulating online disagree with one another, so the advocate must map this citation against the bare Adhiniyam text rather than a table, and record the confirmed section here.
